name: Apple Cider Braised Short Ribs
why: Peak autumn in one Dutch oven: beef short ribs seared hard then braised for three hours in apple cider, red wine and a full bouquet of herbs. Mostly hands-off oven work that rewards you with fall-off-the-bone meat and a naturally sweet, reduced pan sauce.
author: Henry
ingredients: 3-4 lbs (1.4-1.8 kg) bone-in beef short ribs
2 cups (480 ml) apple cider (not apple juice)

steps: Season the short ribs generously with salt and pepper on all sides.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear the ribs in batches until deeply browned on all sides, about 2-3 minutes per side. Remove and set aside — don't rush this step, the browning is your flavour base.
In the same pot, add the onion, carrots and celery. Cook 5-7 minutes until softened and beginning to brown.
Add the garlic and tomato paste and stir for 1 minute.
Deglaze with the apple cider, scraping up the browned bits from the bottom. Simmer 2-3 minutes.
Add the beef broth, red wine, Dijon mustard, thyme, rosemary, bay leaves and cinnamon stick. Stir to combine.
Return the ribs to the pot, nestling them into the liquid and vegetables so the liquid mostly covers the meat.
Cover and braise in the oven for 2.5-3 hours, until the meat is fork-tender and pulling away from the bone.
Remove the pot from the oven and transfer the ribs to a plate. Skim off excess fat from the surface of the liquid.
Optional: simmer the remaining liquid on the stovetop for a few minutes to reduce and thicken the sauce.
Serve hot over mashed potatoes, polenta or crusty bread with a spoonful of the cider sauce.

pro_tips: Use real apple cider (cloudy, unsweetened), not apple juice — the tannins and acidity give the sauce its depth. A 50/50 cider-to-broth ratio keeps it balanced.

Trim most of the fat cap off the ribs before searing but leave a thin layer — it renders into the braise. Skimming the fat from the finished liquid (or chilling and hard-skimming next morning) makes a dramatically cleaner sauce.
